diagnosis.root_cause: The customer's RX optical power has steadily declined from the normal range (about -19.2 dBm) to the degraded range (-26.4 to -27.1 dBm) over seven days. TX power and bias current remain stable, and fibre distance is unchanged, indicating degradation in the customer's fibre path rather than ONU laser ageing, a path change, or shared PON infrastructure failure. The elevated session count is a symptom of the declining optical link.
evidence: The customer's RX telemetry declines continuously from approximately -19.17 dBm, within the normal band, to -26.45 dBm, within the degraded band; this meets the defined declining-link condition.
Live RX is -27.1 dBm, confirming the link is currently degraded.
TX power remains near 2.3 dBm and TX bias current remains stable around 11 mA, which rules out laser degradation.
Distance remains constant at 188 m, ruling out a changed fibre path or record reassignment.
Peers on EPON0/3 have healthy optical levels, so the fault is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON port, splitter or OLT.
The ONU currently responds and is online; the other definite offline ONU on the port is a separate single-ONU offline condition and is consistent with the normal OLT offline background.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP and has normal CPU, memory and temperature, ruling out an OLT or router fault.
The customer's VLAN is correct, the RADIUS entry is present and consistent, and the router heartbeat is healthy.
There are 9 sessions in 24 hours with short average duration, but the optical decline takes precedence; the session instability is a consequence of the degrading fibre link.

remediation.action: Dispatch for physical-layer investigation of the customer's drop fibre and passive path. Clean and reseat ONU, termination, splitter and patch-panel connectors; inspect for bends, damage, contamination or poor splices; perform optical loss/OTDR testing and repair or replace the affected fibre segment, connector or splice. Recheck RX stability and session counts after repair, escalating if RX reaches -28 dBm or lower.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
